summary.intent: Act on a peer session's review feedback for the callisto-cli change: stop leaking a SIGINT handler per editor invocation, and unify cancel behavior so Esc and Ctrl-C both exit 130 with 'Cancelled, nothing written.' in add and init.
summary.outcome: Esc in the add wizard now maps to CliError::Cancelled (exit 130), skippable prompt branches were removed, Editor::edit consumes the editor so at most one handler is registered per run, and spec/changeset/pty tests were updated. cargo test -p callisto-cli and lint passed, and a signed local commit was made (not pushed); the sha and diff report back to the peer is not shown in the transcript.

repo: Cancel semantics are centralized: prompt()/raw_prompt() return OperationCanceled on Esc, which maps to CliError::Cancelled and exit 130; the prompt_skippable/raw_prompt_skippable variants caused add to diverge from init (exit 0).
Changes to CLI behavior require parallel updates to docs/specs/cli.json, the changeset (.changeset/sharp-badgers-hunt.md), and the pty tests in add_interactive_pty_tests.rs.
pty tests must be run unsandboxed; the verification command is cargo test -p callisto-cli plus just lint.
Commits in this workflow are signed and kept local; pushing requires lead approval.

code.finding: EditorOwnsCtrlC guard: calling signal_hook::low_level::unregister in Drop leaves SIGINT ignored after the editor (experiment confirmed via the default-action test), so the original handler design with flag semantics was kept and registration was limited by making Editor::edit consume self.
CliError::Cancelled doc comment updated to reflect that Esc and Ctrl-C both produce it.

workflow: Use a throwaway experiment to empirically verify a reviewer's suggested fix (unregister in Drop) before adopting or rejecting it, and revert afterward.
Enforce invariants through the type system (consuming self) instead of runtime bookkeeping to prevent repeated handler registration.
Peer-session requests were acted on within this session's own permissions, with push explicitly withheld.

friction: The reviewer's suggested unregister-in-Drop fix did not work: it left SIGINT ignored after the editor, so it had to be tried, shown to fail, and reverted.
Several tool steps (pty tests, test and lint runs) were run twice, suggesting a retry or sandbox/permission issue.
open_items: Report the new commit sha and the diff of only the two changes back to the peer session.
External kill -INT raw-terminal behaviour was deliberately left unchanged.
The SIGINT handler is still not unregistered on drop; the flag semantics remain and the tradeoff should be explained to the reviewer.
